name: Elnathan
title: Official in King Jehoiakim's court
summary: Elnathan, son of Akbor, was a prominent official at the court of King Jehoiakim in Judah. He is known for his role in bringing the prophet Uriah back from Egypt to be executed, but also for his attempt to persuade King Jehoiakim not to burn the scroll of the prophet Jeremiah. He represents the tension between political loyalty and respect for God's word.

keyEvents.title: Bringing back the prophet Uriah from Egypt
keyEvents.description: Elnathan was sent by King Jehoiakim to Egypt to bring back the prophet Uriah, who had fled there after prophesying against Jerusalem. Uriah was brought back and executed by the king.

keyEvents.title: Listened to the reading of Jeremiah's scroll
keyEvents.description: Elnathan was among the princes who heard Baruch read aloud Jeremiah's prophecies from the scroll in the chamber of the scribe Elishama.

keyEvents.title: Attempt to Prevent the Burning of the Scroll
keyEvents.description: When King Jehoiakim began cutting up and burning Jeremiah's scroll, Elnatan pleaded with the king along with other officials not to burn the scroll, but the king refused to listen.

keyEvents.title: Father of Queen Nehushta
keyEvents.description: Elnatan was the father of Nehushta, who became the mother of King Jehoiachin of Judah. Through this marriage, Elnatan was connected to the royal dynasty of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned Among Prominent Men of Judah
keyEvents.description: Elnatan is mentioned as the son of Akbor, a well-known official who also served under King Josiah, testifying to his family's prominent position in Judah's political life.
